title: Who walks away when a loved AI app goes bust (derived carousel, carries Mon 9 Nov follow.the.money, piece b358e788)

five_whys.q: Why are Character.AI's users left with nothing?
five_whys.a: The bankruptcy sale takes the staff and the code; Wired reports the bid leaves out users' data, and the filing leaves out the app.

five_whys.q: Why did the buyers want only the staff and code?
five_whys.a: Disney wants its own AI team after OpenAI shut Sora, and buying through the court leaves the lawsuits behind.

five_whys.q: Why did Character.AI end up for sale at all?
five_whys.a: Its founders went to Google in 2024, then lawsuits and a shrinking cash reserve closed in, as the filing says.

five_whys.q: Why is this bigger than one app?
five_whys.a: Big firms are buying their AI makers outright: Netflix bought InterPositive (reported $587 million) and Warner Music bought Sureel AI.

five_whys.q: Why should an everyday business person care?
five_whys.a: Most businesses rent their AI from someone else's company; if that maker is sold or fails, the customer's data and access can go with it, so ask now.

cards.headline: Your AI app can vanish. Ask Character.AI's users
cards.line: Character.AI, where millions chatted with made-up characters, went bust in October. This is what they were left with.
cards.picture: Cover scene: a phone alone on an auction block under a spotlight, a lot tag on it, paper speech bubbles on the floor

cards.headline: Disney is bidding for Character.AI's staff and code.
cards.line: Job offers to 66 staff and the opening $20 million bid for the tech, if the court approves.
cards.picture: 66 small figures and a code block flowing to Disney, a $20M OPENING BID tag

cards.headline: Users were left with an empty shell.
cards.line: The bid leaves out users' data and the app. What happens to their chats is up to the court.
cards.picture: An empty box, chat bubbles drifting out, a tag reading USERS' DATA: NOT IN THE BID

cards.headline: Warning signs showed two years early.
cards.line: Google hired the founders in 2024. Lawsuits followed, and the filing cites a shrinking cash reserve.
cards.picture: A timeline: Aug 2024 founders go to Google, then lawsuits, Oct 2026 bust

cards.headline: Big firms now buy AI makers.
cards.line: Netflix bought the AI film start-up InterPositive, reported at $587 million. Warner Music bought Sureel AI.
cards.picture: RENT to OWN: Disney, Netflix, Warner Music, each with a BOUGHT tag
cards.source: The Hollywood Reporter on Netflix buying InterPositive, reported at $587 million (2026); PR Newswire, Warner Music Group acquires Sureel AI (June 2026)

cards.headline: You rent your AI the same way.
cards.line: If your AI tool's maker is sold or goes bust, your data and access can go with it.
cards.picture: Your business plugged into a socket marked THEIR AI, the socket tagged SOLD? BUST?

cards.headline: Ask your supplier what happens if it's sold.
cards.line: Email it today and get the answer in writing. Then test a backup on one task. Follow for more.
cards.picture: An email to YOUR AI SUPPLIER asking what happens to our data if you're sold, Follow for more over the centred wordmark

read_back.reader: Fresh reader A (Haiku, a small-business owner, headlines only, once; final deck)

answers.what: An AI app's users can lose the app they depend on, as Character.AI's users did.
answers.happened: Disney is bidding for Character.AI's staff and code, and users were left with an empty shell.
answers.why: Big firms are now buying AI makers, so a product can be taken apart in a sale.
answers.so_what: If my AI tool vanishes or changes overnight, I lose the work and the service I rely on.
answers.do: Ask my AI supplier what happens to my access and data if they are sold.

read_back.reader: Fresh reader B (Sonnet, a 15-year-old, headlines only, once; final deck)

answers.what: An AI app like Character.AI can suddenly stop working when a big company buys its parts.
answers.happened: Disney is trying to hire Character.AI's people and take its tech, and users were stuck with an empty app.
answers.why: Big companies buy AI start-ups, and the apps people use are rented, so whoever owns them can change or kill them.
answers.so_what: If I use an AI app, it could disappear and I would lose whatever I built with it.
answers.do: Before I rely on an AI app, ask the company what happens to my stuff if it is sold.

read_back_fixed: Rebuilt 13 Nov on Krish's call ('rebuild monday') around one story, what happened to the people who used Character.AI, after the earlier versions failed the 10/10 judges four times. Read back fresh below. Readers stumbled on whose staff 'its' meant (card 2 now names Character.AI) and which warning signs (card 4's line names them). Judges (6, Instagram) then asked it to open on the reader's own risk; the cover now does. Final readers still asked what the warning signs were (card 4's line names them) and what 'the same way' means (card 6's line says it).
